notes.definition: Different substances may absorb, transmit, refract or reflect electromagnetic waves, and how they do so depends on the wavelength. Refraction is the change in direction of a wave as it crosses a boundary between two media at an angle, caused by the change in the wave's speed.
explanation: When EM waves meet a material, they may be absorbed, transmitted, refracted or reflected, and the effect depends on the wavelength. Glass transmits visible light but absorbs most ultraviolet. The atmosphere transmits visible light and radio waves but absorbs most X-rays and gamma rays from space. Metal reflects microwaves and radio waves. Your body transmits most X-rays but bones absorb them. So a material that is transparent to one type of EM wave may be opaque to another.

Refraction happens because waves travel at different speeds in different substances. Light travels more slowly in glass or water than in air. When light passes from air into glass at an angle to the normal, it slows down and bends towards the normal. When it passes from glass into air it speeds up and bends away from the normal. If the light travels along the normal (at 90° to the boundary) it changes speed but does not change direction. The frequency does not change; the wavelength gets shorter in the slower medium.

To draw a refraction ray diagram: draw the boundary, mark where the ray meets it and draw the normal at 90° to the boundary as a dashed line. Draw the incident ray with an arrow. In the denser (slower) medium, draw the refracted ray closer to the normal, so the angle of refraction is smaller than the angle of incidence. For a rectangular glass block the ray bends towards the normal on entering and away from it on leaving, so it emerges parallel to the incident ray but shifted sideways.

Higher tier students must use wavefront diagrams to explain refraction. A wavefront is a line joining points on the same part of a wave, such as all the crests. When wavefronts reach a boundary at an angle, one end of each wavefront enters the slower medium first and slows down, while the rest is still moving faster. This makes the wavefront change direction. The wavefronts are also closer together in the slower medium because the wavelength is shorter (the frequency is unchanged, so λ = v ÷ f is smaller).

Required practical 10 investigates how the amount of infrared radiation emitted (or absorbed) by a surface depends on the nature of that surface. A Leslie cube has four faces: matt black, shiny black, matt white and shiny silver. It is filled with hot water from a kettle so all faces are at the same temperature. An infrared detector (or thermometer with a blackened bulb) is placed the same distance from each face in turn and the reading is recorded. Matt black emits the most infrared and shiny silver the least. Good emitters are also good absorbers: matt black surfaces absorb the most infrared, while shiny surfaces reflect it.
keyFacts: Substances can absorb, transmit, refract or reflect EM waves, depending on the wavelength.
Refraction is caused by a change in wave speed at a boundary.
Entering a slower (denser) medium at an angle: the ray bends towards the normal.
Entering a faster medium at an angle: the ray bends away from the normal.
A ray along the normal changes speed but not direction.
Frequency stays the same on refraction; wavelength decreases in the slower medium.
Higher: wavefronts change direction because one end slows down before the other.
Required practical 10: matt black emits and absorbs the most infrared; shiny silver the least.
Use the same distance from each face of the Leslie cube for a fair test.

keyTerms.definition: The change in direction of a wave when it crosses a boundary between two media at an angle, due to a change in speed.
A line drawn at 90° to a boundary at the point where a ray meets it.
The angle between the refracted ray and the normal.
A line joining points on a wave that are at the same stage of their oscillation, such as all the crests.
To let a wave pass through a material.
A hollow metal cube with differently finished faces, filled with hot water, used to compare infrared emission.
A sensor that measures the amount of infrared radiation reaching it.

workedExamples.title: Predicting the direction of a refracted ray
workedExamples.question: A ray of light travels from water into air, hitting the surface at 30° to the normal. Light travels faster in air than in water. Describe the path of the ray in air.
steps: The light speeds up as it goes from water into air.
A wave that speeds up at an angle bends away from the normal.
So the angle of refraction in air is greater than 30°.
workedExamples.answer: The ray bends away from the normal, leaving at an angle greater than 30° to the normal.

workedExamples.title: Higher: wavefronts at a boundary
workedExamples.question: Plane wavefronts in deep water reach a boundary with shallow water at an angle. Water waves travel more slowly in shallow water. Explain what happens to the wavefronts.
steps: The end of each wavefront that reaches the shallow water first slows down first.
The rest of the wavefront is still in deep water and keeps moving faster.
This makes each wavefront swing round and change direction, towards the normal.
Frequency stays the same but speed is lower, so the wavelength is shorter and the wavefronts are closer together.
workedExamples.answer: The wavefronts change direction (bend towards the normal) and become closer together.

workedExamples.title: Analysing Leslie cube results
workedExamples.question: A student records these infrared detector readings 10 cm from each face of a Leslie cube: matt black 92, shiny black 75, matt white 70, shiny silver 18 (arbitrary units). State the conclusion and identify the control variables.
steps: Rank the readings: matt black > shiny black > matt white > shiny silver.
Conclusion: matt black is the best emitter of infrared and shiny silver is the worst. Matt surfaces emit more than shiny ones, and dark surfaces more than light ones.
Control variables: same water temperature for all faces (one cube), same distance from detector (10 cm), same detector.
workedExamples.answer: Matt black emits most infrared and shiny silver least; temperature, distance and detector are controlled.

misconceptions.wrong: Students often think light always bends when it crosses a boundary.
misconceptions.right: In fact light travelling along the normal changes speed but not direction. It only changes direction if it meets the boundary at an angle.

misconceptions.wrong: Students often think the frequency of light changes when it is refracted.
misconceptions.right: In fact the frequency stays the same; the speed and wavelength change.

misconceptions.wrong: Students often think a material is either transparent or opaque to all EM waves.
misconceptions.right: In fact it depends on wavelength: glass transmits visible light but absorbs much ultraviolet; walls block light but transmit radio waves.

misconceptions.wrong: Students often think shiny surfaces are good emitters because they look bright.
misconceptions.right: In fact shiny silver surfaces are poor emitters and poor absorbers of infrared; they are good reflectors.

realWorld: Lenses in glasses, cameras and the eye use refraction to focus light.
The atmosphere absorbs harmful X-rays and much ultraviolet from space but transmits visible light and radio waves, so X-ray telescopes must be placed in space.
Emergency foil blankets are shiny so they emit little infrared, keeping a casualty warm.
Houses in hot countries are often painted white to absorb less infrared from the Sun.
higherTier: Use wavefront diagrams to explain refraction in terms of the change of speed that happens when a wave travels from one medium to a different medium.
examTips: In refraction diagrams always draw the normal (dashed) and measure angles from it.
Remember: slows down → bends towards the normal; speeds up → bends away.
Higher: when explaining refraction with wavefronts, say that one part (end) of the wavefront slows down before the rest.
For required practical 10, state the control variables: same temperature (same hot water in one cube), same distance between detector and face, same detector.
Explain why a Leslie cube is used: all faces are at the same temperature at the same time, so only the type of surface changes.
summary: Materials absorb, transmit, refract or reflect EM waves depending on wavelength.
Refraction is caused by a change in speed.
Slower medium: bends towards normal; faster: bends away.
Along the normal: no change in direction.
Higher: wavefronts change direction because one end slows first.
Required practical 10: matt black is the best emitter and absorber of infrared.

A change in the speed of the wave as it crosses a boundary between two media.

flashcards.back: A line joining points on a wave at the same stage of oscillation, e.g. all the crests.

questions.question: What is refraction?
options: The bouncing of a wave off a surface
The absorption of a wave by a material
The change in direction of a wave as it crosses a boundary at an angle
The spreading out of a wave from a source
markScheme: 1 mark: The change in direction of a wave as it crosses a boundary at an angle
questions.explanation: Refraction is a change in direction caused by a change in speed at a boundary. Bouncing back is reflection.

questions.question: A ray of light passes from air into a glass block at an angle. Which way does it bend?
options: Towards the normal
Away from the normal
Along the boundary
It does not bend
markScheme: 1 mark: Towards the normal
questions.explanation: Light slows down in glass, so it bends towards the normal.

questions.question: Which surface is the best emitter of infrared radiation?
options: Shiny silver
Matt white
Shiny white
Matt black
markScheme: 1 mark: Matt black
questions.explanation: Matt black surfaces emit (and absorb) the most infrared. Shiny silver is the worst emitter.

questions.question: What is the cause of refraction?
options: The wave changes frequency when it enters a different medium
The wave changes speed when it enters a different medium
The wave is partly absorbed at the boundary
The wave reflects off the boundary
markScheme: 1 mark: The wave changes speed when it enters a different medium
questions.explanation: Refraction is due to the difference in the speed of the waves in different substances. Frequency does not change.

questions.question: A ray of light hits a glass block along the normal. What happens?
options: It bends towards the normal
It slows down but does not change direction
It bends away from the normal
It is totally reflected
markScheme: 1 mark: It slows down but does not change direction
questions.explanation: Along the normal the angle of incidence is 0°, so although the light slows down, it does not change direction.

questions.question: Which statement about glass and EM waves is correct?
options: Glass transmits all types of EM wave equally
Glass reflects all infrared radiation
Glass absorbs visible light but transmits gamma rays only
Glass transmits visible light but absorbs much ultraviolet
markScheme: 1 mark: Glass transmits visible light but absorbs much ultraviolet
questions.explanation: How a substance affects EM waves depends on wavelength. Ordinary glass transmits visible light but absorbs much of the UV, which is why you are less likely to get sunburnt through a window.

questions.question: In required practical 10, why is an infrared detector placed the same distance from each face of the Leslie cube?
options: To make it a fair test, since the reading depends on distance
To keep the water at the same temperature
To stop the detector getting too hot
Because the detector only works at one distance
markScheme: 1 mark: To make it a fair test, since the reading depends on distance
questions.explanation: The amount of infrared reaching the detector decreases with distance. Keeping the distance the same means only the surface type affects the reading.

questions.question: A Leslie cube is filled with hot water. Which explains why it gives a fairer comparison of surfaces than four separate cans of hot water?
options: The cube cools down more slowly than cans
The cube has a larger volume of water
All four faces are at the same temperature at the same time
The cube's faces are all made of different metals
markScheme: 1 mark: All four faces are at the same temperature at the same time
questions.explanation: One cube means one water temperature for all faces. With four cans, the water temperatures might differ and cool at different rates.

questions.question: Wavefronts travel from deep water into shallow water, where they move more slowly. Which statement is correct?
options: The wavefronts get further apart and their frequency increases
The wavefronts keep the same spacing but slow down
The wavefronts' frequency decreases so they get closer together
The wavefronts get closer together and change direction if they arrive at an angle
markScheme: 1 mark: The wavefronts get closer together and change direction if they arrive at an angle
questions.explanation: Frequency is unchanged; slower speed means shorter wavelength, so wavefronts are closer together. Arriving at an angle, one end slows first so they change direction.

questions.question: Using a wavefront diagram, why does a wave bend towards the normal when it enters a slower medium at an angle?
options: The whole wavefront slows down at the same instant
The wavefronts reflect off the boundary first
One end of each wavefront slows down before the rest of the wavefront
The frequency of the wavefront decreases on one side
markScheme: 1 mark: One end of each wavefront slows down before the rest of the wavefront
questions.explanation: The part of the wavefront that crosses the boundary first moves more slowly, while the rest continues at the faster speed. This swings the wavefront round, changing its direction.

questions.question: Name two things, other than refraction, that can happen when EM waves meet a substance.
markScheme: 1 mark each for any two of: absorbed, transmitted, reflected
questions.explanation: Substances may absorb, transmit, refract or reflect EM waves.

questions.question: Describe what happens to a ray of light as it passes from glass into air at an angle to the normal.
markScheme: 1 mark: it speeds up
1 mark: it bends away from the normal
questions.explanation: Leaving glass into air the light speeds up, so it bends away from the normal and the angle of refraction is larger than the angle of incidence.

questions.question: Required practical 10. State the independent variable and the dependent variable when using a Leslie cube.
markScheme: 1 mark: independent: type of surface (colour / texture of face)
1 mark: dependent: amount of infrared radiation emitted / detector reading
questions.explanation: The surface is changed on purpose; the infrared reading is measured.

questions.question: Required practical 10. Explain why the readings should be taken quickly once the hot water is added to the Leslie cube.
markScheme: 1 mark: the water cools down over time
1 mark: so later faces would be at a lower temperature and emit less, making the comparison unfair
questions.explanation: Taking all readings close together keeps the temperature as similar as possible for each face.

questions.question: State what happens to the frequency of light when it is refracted.
markScheme: 1 mark: it stays the same / does not change
questions.explanation: Frequency is set by the source. Speed and wavelength change on refraction.

questions.question: Higher: explain, using the idea of wavefronts, why light changes direction when it enters glass from air at an angle.
acceptedAnswers: wavefront reaches boundary at an angle
markScheme: 1 mark: the wavefront meets the boundary at an angle, so one end / part enters the glass first
1 mark: that part slows down while the rest is still travelling faster in air
1 mark: so the wavefront changes direction (bends towards the normal)
questions.explanation: Different parts of the wavefront travel at different speeds for a short time, which turns the wavefront.

questions.question: Suggest why X-ray telescopes are placed on satellites rather than on the ground.
acceptedAnswers: X-rays do not reach the ground
markScheme: 1 mark: the atmosphere absorbs X-rays
1 mark: so X-rays from space do not reach the ground / a telescope above the atmosphere can detect them
questions.explanation: The way a substance affects EM waves depends on wavelength: air transmits visible light but absorbs X-rays.

questions.question: Describe how to draw a ray diagram to show light refracting as it passes from air into a glass block.
markScheme: Indicative content:
draw the boundary and mark the point where the incident ray meets it
draw the normal at 90° to the boundary as a dashed line
draw the incident ray with an arrow, at an angle to the normal
draw the refracted ray in the glass closer to the normal (angle of refraction smaller than angle of incidence)
label angles of incidence and refraction measured from the normal
light slows down in glass
Level 2 (3 to 4 marks): clear description including the normal and correct direction of bending.
Level 1 (1 to 2 marks): some correct features but bending direction or normal missing.
questions.explanation: Key points: normal at 90°, angles measured from the normal, bends towards the normal in glass.

questions.question: Required practical 10. Describe a method to investigate how the type of surface affects the amount of infrared radiation emitted. Include how you would make the investigation valid and the results you would expect.
markScheme: Indicative content:
use a Leslie cube with matt black, shiny black, matt white and shiny silver faces
fill with hot water from a kettle (take care: scalding risk)
place an infrared detector (or thermometer with blackened bulb) a fixed distance, e.g. 10 cm, from one face
record the reading, then turn the cube so each face faces the detector in turn at the same distance
take readings quickly so the water temperature stays about the same
control: same distance, same detector, same temperature, same size of face
repeat and calculate a mean
expected: matt black emits most, shiny silver least; dark and matt surfaces emit more than light and shiny ones
Level 3 (5 to 6 marks): coherent method that would produce valid results with control variables and correct expected results.
Level 2 (3 to 4 marks): workable method with some control variables or expected results.
Level 1 (1 to 2 marks): simple statements; method lacks detail.
questions.explanation: A strong answer names the apparatus, controls distance and temperature, and states that matt black emits the most infrared.

questions.question: Higher: water waves in a ripple tank travel from deep water into shallow water, where they are slower. The wavefronts meet the boundary at an angle. Describe and explain what happens to the wavefronts.
markScheme: Indicative content:
speed decreases in shallow water
frequency stays the same
so wavelength decreases: wavefronts closer together
one end of each wavefront reaches the shallow water first and slows down first
rest of the wavefront still moving faster
so wavefronts change direction, bending towards the normal
Level 2 (3 to 4 marks): explains both the change in spacing and change in direction in terms of speed.
Level 1 (1 to 2 marks): states that waves slow down or change direction without full explanation.
questions.explanation: This is the same physics as light entering glass, shown with water waves.

questions.question: In a ray diagram, what is drawn at 90° to the boundary where a ray hits it?
options: The refracted ray
The normal
The incident ray
The wavefront
markScheme: 1 mark: The normal
questions.explanation: The normal is a dashed construction line at 90° to the boundary. Angles of incidence and refraction are measured from it.

questions.question: Which surface is the best absorber of infrared radiation?
options: Matt black
Shiny silver
Shiny white
Polished aluminium
markScheme: 1 mark: Matt black
questions.explanation: Good emitters are good absorbers: matt black absorbs the most infrared. Shiny surfaces reflect most infrared.

questions.question: State what happens to the speed of light when it passes from air into water.
markScheme: 1 mark: it decreases / slows down
questions.explanation: Light travels more slowly in water than in air, which is why it refracts at the surface.

questions.question: Required practical 10. Name a piece of equipment that could be used to measure the infrared radiation emitted by each face of a Leslie cube.
markScheme: 1 mark: infrared detector (allow thermopile or thermometer with a blackened bulb)
questions.explanation: An infrared detector gives a reading that increases with the amount of infrared reaching it.

questions.question: Required practical 10. Identify one hazard in this practical and state a precaution.
markScheme: 1 mark: hazard: hot water / hot cube can scald or burn
1 mark: precaution: pour carefully, do not touch the hot cube, place on a heatproof mat, wipe up spills
questions.explanation: Boiling water from a kettle is the main hazard.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a way a substance can affect an EM wave?
options: Absorb it
Transmit it
Increase its speed in a vacuum
Reflect it
markScheme: 1 mark: Increase its speed in a vacuum
questions.explanation: Substances can absorb, transmit, refract or reflect EM waves. Nothing changes the speed of EM waves in a vacuum, which is always 3 × 10⁸ m/s.

questions.question: A ray of light enters a rectangular glass block at an angle and leaves through the opposite parallel face. How does the emerging ray compare with the incident ray?
options: It is parallel to the incident ray but shifted sideways
It continues along exactly the same line as the incident ray
It is bent towards the normal compared with the incident ray
It travels back towards the source
markScheme: 1 mark: It is parallel to the incident ray but shifted sideways
questions.explanation: It bends towards the normal on entering and by the same amount away from the normal on leaving, so it emerges parallel to its original direction but displaced sideways.
